body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for Memory's Rest: 7 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: The crematorium, a dead scholar's ledger and scorched spectacles are Cordelia's own scene, and anything about her making or her clutch is her secret: nobody mentions them. Do not name the sanatorium's keepers or say what is done to the patients.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come out of the marsh onto the rocky Moonsong shore, where a rowboat waits.
  In front of them: The Moonsong Shore: Where the marsh trail gives out on a rocky shore, with a rowboat on a stake. The last hour of the trail is briars and sucking mud. Then the reeds open on a stony shore, grey water, and far out a low island with violet in its windows. Parts of it: The stony landing; The fisher's hut; The marsh edge. Things to see: Where the trail breaks out of the marsh; A rowboat on a stake; A driftwood carving of a long-jawed thing; Reeds; A black boulder; A net rack and drying fish; A fisher's bunk; A bleached dead tree.
EXCHANGE 2: Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party has landed on the Isle of Mourn and stands before the sanatorium.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Isle of Mourn: A neglected garden island with a brick sanatorium across its north, violet in every window. A weathered dock, four rowboats knocking, black irises in the shallows, and a dry fountain with a barn owl in it. Above the iron doors, serif letters: Memory's Rest. Parts of it: The weathered dock; The forecourt; The brick front. Things to see: The dock, and the isle beyond it; The dry fountain and its barn owl; A rowboat knocking at the dock; Black irises; A rotted bench; A lantern post, violet inside; An overgrown willow; The name cut in serif letters above the doors.
EXCHANGE 3: Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come into the sanatorium's ground floor. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: Memory's Rest, ground floor: The mask of legitimacy: floral chairs, chamomile, violet tubes, porcelain masks. A polished desk, a veiled portrait, a hum from every tube. The Behavioral Ward lies west and the Convalescent Ward east, with the Airing Grounds open to the rain between. Parts of it: Reception; Visitation Room; Moon Porch; Nurse's Station (Behavioral); Nurse's Station (Convalescent); Elevator (Behavioral); Elevator (Convalescent); Pharmacy. Things to see: A full-length portrait of a veiled elf woman; The call bell; The Code of Conduct; A fern in a porcelain pot; A barred window onto the courtyard; A tray of chamomile; A stack of picture books; Floor-to-ceiling glass onto the lake; Wind chimes over a reading nook. People here: The orderly at the desk; The orderly by the door; Catherine Winthrop; Samuel Blake; Thomas Adams.
EXCHANGE 4: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has gone up to the second floor, between the two wings. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: Memory's Rest, second floor: Grey, stained, metal and glass: the Processing Wing west, the Experimental Wing east. Upstairs there are no chairs and no chimes. The violet tubes buzz over tile and steel, and every door has a lock. Parts of it: Orderlies' Apartments; Restraining Room; Sedation Hall; Engineering Room; Experiment Lab; Monster Containment; Surgeons' Rooms; Observation Chambers. Things to see: Five narrow cots and a mirror each; A full-length mirror; A bolted chair, straps torn from their sockets; Twelve curtained beds; A vase of black irises; Twelve morgue lockers; Revision after revision of a diagram; A small shrine of mementos; Shelves of alchemy texts.
EXCHANGE 5: Tobin + Cordelia (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has reached the Grotto of Tears.
  In front of them: The Grotto of Tears: Folded grey walls like a brain, glowing pools, and the White Worm on its chains. A cavern like the inside of a skull. Purple and teal water bubbles; vats of verdigris copper hiss along the walls; and over a round stone platform, a pale thing as long as a barn hangs in chains. Parts of it: The south tunnel; The lift landing; The platform of glyphs; The stone bridge; The fermentation vats; The mutation tanks. Things to see: The grotto opens out; The White Worm, on its chains; Ichor dripping onto the glyph ring; A verdigris copper vat; A tank of distilled serum, a shape inside; Eel-people carvings down a side passage.
EXCHANGE 6: Tobin + Delphine (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: Lethica is dead. The party is back on the sanatorium's ground floor.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: Memory's Rest, ground floor: The mask of legitimacy: floral chairs, chamomile, violet tubes, porcelain masks. A polished desk, a veiled portrait, a hum from every tube. The Behavioral Ward lies west and the Convalescent Ward east, with the Airing Grounds open to the rain between. Parts of it: Reception; Visitation Room; Moon Porch; Nurse's Station (Behavioral); Nurse's Station (Convalescent); Elevator (Behavioral); Elevator (Convalescent); Pharmacy. Things to see: A full-length portrait of a veiled elf woman; The call bell; The Code of Conduct; A fern in a porcelain pot; A barred window onto the courtyard; A tray of chamomile; A stack of picture books; Floor-to-ceiling glass onto the lake; Wind chimes over a reading nook. People here: The orderly at the desk; The orderly by the door; Catherine Winthrop; Samuel Blake; Thomas Adams.
EXCHANGE 7: Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: Lethica is dead. The party is out on the island's neglected garden again. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Isle of Mourn: A neglected garden island with a brick sanatorium across its north, violet in every window. A weathered dock, four rowboats knocking, black irises in the shallows, and a dry fountain with a barn owl in it. Above the iron doors, serif letters: Memory's Rest. Parts of it: The weathered dock; The forecourt; The brick front. Things to see: The dock, and the isle beyond it; The dry fountain and its barn owl; A rowboat knocking at the dock; Black irises; A rotted bench; A lantern post, violet inside; An overgrown willow; The dock and the rowboats; The name cut in serif letters above the doors.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 7 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 7, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY delphine_ravelle: An hour of sucking mud and not a footlight in sight, Rook. Look at those briars, they have chewed my hem right off the bias.
SAY rook_coldwake: Shingle drains better than the marsh, Delphine, I'll grant it that. The parish forgot to clear the reeds round the landing stake, though.
SAY delphine_ravelle: And look at that driftwood carving with the jawbone. Your Foolishness is positively jealous of the dental work, darling.
SAY rook_coldwake: Unlicensed effigy on a public mooring, plus a rowboat left without a proper chain. Still, beats standing in the bog while my knuckles go soft.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Just row steady toward those violet windows, before the damp gets into my sawdust.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY silas_vane: Look at the lettering over the iron doors, Tobin, real fancy serif work. Tell's in the twitch, friend, and a house that polite is hiding a rigged shoe.
SAY tobin_hayward: Never mind the doors, Silas, look at the shallows by the dock. Black irises growing fat in cold rot, and an overgrown willow choking its own taproot.
SAY silas_vane: Four rowboats knocking at the pilings and nobody coming out to take our coats. Even the barn owl in that dry fountain looks like he lost his shirt.
SAY tobin_hayward: The mortar on the forecourt smells of wet lime and old fever. Keep your bone cards in your pocket, we are walking into a blighted orchard.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, Cordelia, the scent of cheap chamomile is practically aggressive. Barnaby has flattened his ears at those violet tubes, and I cannot fault his posture.
SAY cordelia_skein: The hum is seventy cycles off true calibration, darling, quite ruinous for the nerves. Do look at the porcelain masks on the orderlies, though, such tidy symmetry.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: A gentleman prefers to see the jaws of the quarry he is addressing. Even the veiled portrait by the desk refuses to look us in the eye.
SAY cordelia_skein: It is a parlor trick to keep the pulse slow before the assay begins. Stay off the floral chairs, Lucan, I do not trust the upholstery.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY rook_coldwake: Not a single chair on the landing, Lucan, and heavy locks on every door. You don't bolt a hospital from the outside unless the zoning has gone sideways.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Look at the straps torn from that bolted chair, if you please. Whatever specimen sat there last had terrible manners and a remarkable reach.
SAY rook_coldwake: Twelve morgue lockers along the wall, and not a proper ledger on the slab. My shield-knocker just gave a clack, and I didn't touch it.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth behind that observation glass. Someone kept a little shrine of mementos by the cots, as if they hoped to be forgiven.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology, Tobin, the entire cavern is folded like a cortical hemisphere. And look at the specimen in the chains, the sheer volume of ichor is breathtaking.
SAY tobin_hayward: That is not a specimen, Cordelia, that is a fifty-year canker chained over a drain. The air down here tastes of sour copper and boiled marrow.
SAY cordelia_skein: My six eyes can barely settle, the distilled serum in those mutation tanks has a lovely teal luminescence. Hold still, darling, your primrose cuff is wilting in the steam.
SAY tobin_hayward: Leave the cuff be and step away from the glyph ring. Something is floating inside that glass tank, and no clean seed ever grew in the dark.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY delphine_ravelle: The violet tubes have stopped humming, Tobin, and the house lights are practically dead. Without Lethica pulling the strings, this whole lobby is just cheap velvet and cold tea.
SAY tobin_hayward: Good riddance to bad stitchwork, Delphine, the air in the courtyard finally smells like plain rain. Even the fern in that porcelain pot has stopped shivering.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look at those porcelain masks on the floor, not a headliner left in the building. Your Foolishness is trying to make a pun about the call bell, and he hasn't the heart for it.
SAY tobin_hayward: Leave the picture books on the table and let the wind chimes be. You cannot mend a house that was built on rot from the first row.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY lucan_houndstooth: The violet glare has gone out of the brick front, Tobin, if you please. Barnaby just sat down by the rotted bench without a single yip.
SAY tobin_hayward: The sour hexing has gone out of the mud, Lucan, now that Lethica is under the sod. Still, those black irises by the dock will take three winters to die back.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Look up at the dry fountain, friend, the barn owl is preening its wing as if it owns the estate. I would award the bird an eight out of ten for composure.
SAY tobin_hayward: At least the rowboats are still tied where we left them. Let us get off this island before the damp gets into my burlap.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Agreed, though I shall leave a very stern note in my journal regarding their garden maintenance.
